clue.text: Vindictiveness displayed by mother stepping, on household pests

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece stepping on another sits above it, so the mother word comes first

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for one's mother
lice are small parasitic pests found about the home

explanation.surface: A mother's spite comes out as she stamps on the bugs infesting the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm others, which is exactly what vindictiveness amounts to.

clue.text: Don't flag-leave it at the masthead

explanation.surface: An order not to lower the flag from the top of the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping going without tiring is not flagging, and a flag kept hoisted stays at the top of the mast.

clue.text: Inconclusive story constantly repeated by a bore

explanation.surface: A dull talker keeps telling the same unfinished yarn over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A story without an ending is literally unending, and a bore's tale that goes on and on feels interminable.

clue.text: Permanently fix on the floor of the theatre

parts.note: being on the floor of a theatre is being in it, so on gives IN
the stalls are the seats on the ground floor of a theatre; one seat there is a stall

explanation.surface: A fitting to be fixed in place on the theatre's ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to set it in position for lasting use.

clue.text: Rochester's state restored on the other side of the road

definitions.text: on the other side of the road

indicators.note: restored suggests putting the letters back together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The city of Rochester has had its old condition brought back, opposite the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses every letter of ROCHESTERS (the 's counts here) and STATE; 'restored' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something across the street is situated opposite, beyond the roadway.

clue.text: Sacrifice on behalf of oneself

parts.note: doing something for someone is acting on their behalf
the ego is the self, one's own sense of identity

explanation.surface: Giving something up for one's own benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: FOREGO is a recognised variant spelling of forgo.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to do without something, giving it up willingly.

clue.text: Deer found in North India

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters lie inside the words North India

explanation.surface: A kind of deer that lives in northern India.
explanation.definitionFit: A hind is a female red deer.

clue.text: When hunted would it be unable to run?

definitions.text: When hunted would it be unable to run?

parts.words: When hunted would it be unable to run?
parts.note: plays on the word for hunted animals also meaning lame, as in a crippled leg that cannot run

explanation.surface: A question about whether a hunted creature could escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals pursued for sport are game, and a lame leg is called a game leg.

clue.text: One confused era

indicators.note: confused tells us to jumble the letters of the word One

explanation.surface: A single muddled period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long age, a span of time like an era.

clue.text: To stop argument leave the matter on ice for a while

definitions.text: leave the matter on ice for a while

explanation.surface: Advice to end a quarrel by putting the issue on hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling people to calm down ends a row, and literally chilling something is leaving it on ice.

clue.text: Easy remedy

explanation.surface: A straightforward cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple means uncomplicated; a simple is also an old term for a medicinal herb or the cure made from it.

clue.text: They are better than one device for always winning the toss

definitions.text: device for always winning the toss

explanation.surface: A gimmick for winning coin tosses beats a single attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a pair of minds beats one, and a double-headed coin always comes down the caller's way when they call heads.

clue.text: Get even a box seat to take ancient musical manuscripts

parts.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench, often with a box under the seat
ancient means old
scores are written copies of music

explanation.surface: A bench is brought in to hold some antique sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling old scores means taking revenge for past wrongs.

clue.text: Sheep found in Nigeria

explanation.surface: A sheep living in Nigeria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ewe are a West African people, chiefly of Ghana and Togo; the clue loosely places them in Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a ewe, and the Ewe are also a West African people and their language.

clue.text: Weapon which disabled poor Ted

indicators.note: disabled suggests something broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weapon that put unfortunate Ted out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile.

clue.text: Admit to being in possession

explanation.surface: Confessing to having something.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, and to own is to possess.

clue.text: Racing dog most likely to beat the favourite

parts.note: to whip is to beat
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Tipping a greyhound to outrun the race favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slim, fast breed used in dog racing.

clue.text: All the money from the sale goes

definitions.text: All the money from the sale

explanation.surface: Takings from a sale disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are the money raised by a sale, and to proceed is to go on.

clue.text: Rich hob cooked yeast cake

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

parts.note: the printed words are the anagram fodder, which as the setter meant it gives RICH plus OBE (a slip put a second H in place of the E)

explanation.surface: A rich cake baked on the hob.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'Rich hob' has two Hs and no E, so 'cooked' cannot make the cake; the setter's fodder should give RICH plus OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioche is a light sweet French bread made from yeast dough enriched with butter and eggs.

clue.text: Disembodied saint presents no ready answer

indicators.note: disembodied suggests the words broken up and rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: A ghostly saint appears but has no quick reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply given immediately is a ready answer.

clue.text: A knightly habit, thanks to Shakespeare

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: Thanks to Shakespeare, we know about knights' garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is the short tunic a knight wore over armour, bearing his arms; habit here means clothing.

clue.text: Advice to shop-keeper whose loquacity has driven away his custom

definitions.text: Advice to shop-keeper whose loquacity has driven away his custom

parts.words: Advice to shop-keeper whose loquacity has driven away his custom
parts.note: a talkative trader should stop talking, and having lost all customers he may as well close the shop

explanation.surface: A chatty shopkeeper has talked his customers away.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to be quiet and telling a trader to close the business use the same phrase.

parts.note: four is a pair multiplied by a pair, and 22 is a pair of digits standing side by side

explanation.surface: A puzzle about two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes multiplication of a pair by a pair and also things going in pairs, like animals into the Ark.

clue.text: War office advertisement for old war paint

parts.note: WO is the abbreviation for the War Office, the former British army ministry

explanation.surface: A military recruiting poster promoting ancient battle paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Woad is a blue dye from a plant, which ancient Britons painted on their bodies for battle.

clue.text: Monkey rushes all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place suggests scattered letters that must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey dashing about everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a brown monkey of South and East Asia.

clue.text: Bay named by Hardy's companion

explanation.surface: A bay tree named after a friend of the novelist Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is also called sweet bay or bay laurel, and Stan Laurel partnered Oliver Hardy in comedy films.

clue.text: Shady city of Vietnam

explanation.surface: A dubious Vietnamese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Shady plays on shade: a colour's shade is a hue, so the word is a punning stand-in rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint or shade of colour is a hue, and Hue is the old imperial capital in central Vietnam.

clue.text: Old copper carpeted for illegal merchandise

parts.note: D stands for the old British penny, a copper coin
carpeted suggests having a rug laid down, giving the floor covering

explanation.surface: A retired policeman is reprimanded over contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics trafficked unlawfully are illicit goods traded on the black market.
